subject: Throughput sizing follow-up / Performance SLOs (post-call)
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Priya Rao <priya@finex.com>, Alan Chen <alan@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput sizing follow-up / Performance SLOs (post-call)

Thanks again for the call this morning — really helpful to see the traffic patterns and the three usage modes you described. Below is my read of the perf/throughput requirements and the next steps so we can produce a concrete sizing and an initial Dedicated proposal. Please correct anything I got wrong.

Summary of requirements (as discussed):
- Latency targets: P95 end-to-end <= 250 ms for 512-token responses (streaming enabled).
- Concurrency: ~80 steady concurrent active sessions for the primary flow; up to 250 concurrent sessions during peak campaigns.
- QPS / request rate: steady-state ~60 requests/sec; typical peak bursts up to 200 requests/sec for short windows (~10-15 minutes).
- Average payloads: prompt ~60 tokens, generation up to 512 tokens (average gen 200 tokens, sometimes up to 512 for long replies).
- Tokens/sec (client-visible): steady ~16k tokens/sec (60 rps * ~260 tokens), peak bursts ~52k tokens/sec (200 rps * ~260 tokens).
- Streaming: required — partial tokens must be delivered as generated for UX.
- SLA needs: 99.9% availability during business hours; cost sensitivity secondary to latency for the first phase.

Open clarifications we asked for on the call (action items for Finex):
1) 7-day representative trace (jsonl) of requests with timestamps, payload sizes (prompt + gen), and concurrent session markers.
2) Confirmation if the 250ms P95 is strict across all endpoints or only for the primary conversational route.
3) Which endpoints require streaming vs batch responses.

What Redwood will deliver next:
- Initial throughput sizing workbook (attached) with conservative and optimized configurations.
- Proposed canary plan for a Dedicated deployment and suggested rollout (canary -> 25% -> 100%).
- SRE sync to capture traces and run a short load test with a synthetic workload mirroring your traces.

Attachments: redwood_throughput_workbook.xlsx (initial sizing workbook / assumptions).

Can we agree on the following next steps?
- Finex: share 7-day traces + confirm strictness of the 250ms P95 target by Tue 2026-03-31 EOD.
- Redwood: we’ll review traces and propose an initial Dedicated capacity and a follow-up SRE call by Wed 2026-04-01.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com

From: Priya Rao <priya@finex.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: Alan Chen <alan@finex.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Mar 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing follow-up / Performance SLOs (post-call)

Thanks Rafael — that summary looks good overall. A couple of clarifications from our side:
- Latency: we actually want to target P95 <= 200 ms for the primary conversational endpoint. For secondary endpoints (analytics batch scoring) 500 ms P95 is acceptable.
- Average gen length: closer to 200 tokens for conversation; occasional long-form outputs up to 512 tokens (~5% of traffic).
- Steady QPS: it's more like 50-60 rps; peaks are sometimes higher than discussed — we can see short bursts up to 300 rps during promos, but those are <10 minutes.
- Concurrency: steady ~80, but we need headroom to ~300 concurrent sessions during those promo bursts.
- Streaming: yes, streaming is required for the primary UX (progressive rendering).

We’ll pull the 7-day traces and anonymize user identifiers — plan to share by EOD Tue (2026-03-31).

Priya Rao
Head of Platform, Finex
priya@finex.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Priya Rao <priya@finex.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing follow-up / Performance SLOs (post-call)

Hi Priya — thanks for the quick clarifications. Based on Rafael’s workbook and the updated numbers you provided, I’ve put together an initial sizing estimate (see attached PDF) and a short plan for the SRE sync. High level sizing callouts:
- Baseline steady-state: target P95 <= 200 ms for primary endpoint -> estimated Dedicated capacity: 6 x A100-equivalent GPUs with optimized batching and prefix caching. This covers ~60 rps steady and ~80 steady concurrency with streaming and low latency.
- Burst capacity: for short peaks up to 300 rps / ~300 concurrent sessions, we recommend a burst pool (auto-scale to add 8 GPUs for 10–15 minute windows) or routing bursts to a cheaper non-streaming variant with slightly higher latency if you can tolerate it for promos.
- Tokens/sec: steady ~13k–16k tokens/sec; peak planning up to ~78k tokens/sec (accounting for larger gen lengths during promos).
- Streaming considerations: streaming increases CPU networking overhead; we’ll reserve extra egress headroom in the canary profile.

Action items I’ll take:
- Review traces once you upload and adjust the workbook assumptions.
- Propose a 60-minute SRE sync (Wed 2026-04-01 10:00 AM PT) to validate traces and run a short synthetic load test.

Attachment: initial_sizing_estimate.pdf (notes + GPU-count recommendations).

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Perfect — thanks Priya and Marissa. Confirming next steps:
- Finex (Priya): upload 7-day anonymized traces + a couple of representative payloads by Tue EOD (2026-03-31).
- Redwood (Marissa / Neha / Rafael): review traces and present an updated sizing + cost estimate after the SRE sync.
- SRE sync: Wed 2026-04-01 10:00 AM PT (calendar invite to follow).

If you could also flag any endpoints that absolutely cannot be re-routed to a higher-latency path during promos, that will help us size the burst strategy.

I’ll send the invite and a short agenda now.

Thanks — Rafael
